chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn Razīn, from Dharīḥ al-Muḥāribī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whom one person wounded with a muḍiḥah wound and another wounded with a dāmiyah wound in a single incident, and then the man died. He عليه السلام said: "The diyah is upon both of them from their property, in two equal halves."

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money or financial compensation for unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.فِي أَمْوَالِهِمَا نِصْفَيْنِ: from their own wealth, divided into two equal halves
key_terms.فِي مَقَامٍ وَاحِدٍ: in one and the same incident or situation
key_terms.مُوضِحَةً: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: If two people inflict different wounds on one man and he dies, how is the diyah divided?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning joint liability when two people inflict separate head wounds on one victim in the same incident and the victim dies. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the diyah is due from both offenders equally, each bearing half from his own wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5383 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Salih ibn Razin, from Dharih Al-Muharibi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who was struck by one person with a muḍihah wound (a wound that exposes the bone) and by another person with a damiyah wound (a bleeding wound) in the same instance, and the man died.
Imam (as) said: "The blood money is upon both of them, divided equally between their wealth."
